topbar.bridgeHint: The bridge runs on the machine that owns the arm, so its address differs per site — this page never connects to a default; put the site's address here

link.title: VR Link
link.statLatencyNote: The headset clock is not comparable with this host: the value is the increase over the window's minimum, not an absolute latency
link.fallbackBody: No frames for over {{ms}} ms — the bridge sent latch to hold in place. Following resumes only after a fresh grip press.
link.versionMismatchHint: The bridge reports {{version}} while this page is written against {{supported}} — some fields may already be read wrongly. Bring one side up to match.
link.guardOff: Fallback is off (FALLBACK_ENABLED=0 on the bridge): no automatic hold even after {{ms}} ms without new frames
link.rearmHint: Press the right grip again (release → press) to resume following

preview.title: Arm Preview
preview.modelHint: Note: with a **single arm** this view renders the same URDF as the control page (studio/SDK) while the joint angles come from metavr’s own model. The two differ in joint origins, axes and limits, so the picture does not match what metavr believes and the arm looks askew. That is a known deviation, not bad data.
preview.modelHintDual: With two arms this is the rig model (metavr’s dual_litearm_column_description, low-poly meshes): two side-mounted arms on one column, each driven by its own chain of joint angles — what metavr itself believes.

control.title: Teleop Control
control.estopHint: Sends stop to the follow server and stops forwarding controller frames
control.consoleBusyTitle: The console is driving the arm
control.consoleBusyBody: Console side: {{activity}}. VR teleoperation and the console are mutually exclusive links (they cannot share the same motors) — release the console side before starting VR teleoperation.
control.consoleBusyHint: The console (studio → litearm-server :7449) is driving the arm — the two links are mutually exclusive, so VR teleoperation cannot start from here
control.conflictTitle: Both links are driving the arm
control.conflictBody: The bridge reports the VR side is following while the console side is also driving the arm. The two links are mutually exclusive — the same motors cannot be commanded by two controllers. Stop one side now and verify the arm state.
control.rearmHint: Stopped or e-stopped: press grip again to resume following

manifest.title: Arm mapping
manifest.hint: Which serial port is which arm, and which CAN channel its gripper is on — a wrong mapping does not error, it just drives the other arm
manifest.mismatch: The follow server actually opened {{device}} — not the one selected above
manifest.savedNothing: Already what the bridge uses — nothing changed
manifest.portsUnavailable: Could not list candidate ports ({{reason}}) — you can type the port name instead.
manifest.busy: Teleop is running, or an upstream process still is — stop it first (the port is frozen into the command line at start).
manifest.noArms: The bridge has not reported any arm yet — two rows appear once it does.
manifest.gripperMismatch: The gripper service reports {{device}} — not what is selected above
